name: Death and Afterlife

objectives.text: Identify from the Easter account that Jesus died and rose again, defeating death
Name heaven as the place where, Scripture teaches, believers will be with Jesus
Retell how Jesus wept with Mary and Martha and then raised Lazarus from the dead
Explain from Genesis and Romans the biblical teaching that death entered the world through sin
Describe the main parts of a Christian funeral and explain how each expresses both grief and hope
Summarize the Christian teaching that believers will be raised bodily when Christ returns
Explain how the Hindu and Buddhist idea of reincarnation differs from the biblical teaching of one life followed by judgment and resurrection
Compare the funeral and mourning practices of Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, and Christianity and identify the belief about the afterlife that each practice expresses
Explain how 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 shapes the way Christians are taught to grieve and to comfort one another
Explain from Scripture that the final Christian hope is a renewed creation with resurrected bodies and not only a heavenly existence
Analyze the Reformed teaching on the intermediate state in contrast with the doctrines of purgatory and soul sleep
Interpret the terms Sheol and Hades in their Old and New Testament contexts and distinguish them from the final states of heaven and hell
Explain how Scripture presents the resurrection of Christ as the firstfruits and guarantee of the future resurrection of believers
Compare a secular naturalist view of death as final extinction with the Christian hope of resurrection and the reasons each gives for how to live
Explain the doctrine of the last judgment as taught in Scripture and the Westminster Confession
Explain why Reformed churches do not pray for the dead and contrast this with practices of prayer for the dead and ancestor veneration in other traditions
Compare annihilationism with eternal conscious punishment, the view of the Reformed confessions, by examining the key passages each view cites
Analyze Islamic teaching on death, the grave, and judgment by deeds in comparison with the Christian teaching that believers are judged as justified in Christ
Construct a biblical theology of death as an enemy that Christ has defeated and will finally destroy
Evaluate claims drawn from near-death experiences by the standard of Scripture's sufficiency
Evaluate common objections to the doctrine of hell and defend its consistency with the justice of God as the Reformed tradition teaches it
Evaluate arguments for euthanasia and assisted suicide in light of the sixth commandment and the biblical teaching that God governs life and death
Compose a short funeral meditation that expounds 1 Corinthians 15:54-57 for a grieving congregation

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Christ's victory over death, heaven, resurrection hope, funerals, reincarnation contrast, 1 Thessalonians 4 grief, intermediate state, Sheol and Hades, firstfruits, annihilationism, death as enemy, NDEs, hell and justice, 1 Corinthians 15:55). Replaced 'observe that funerals are sad' with describing funeral elements, removed feeling-based wording, and turned the final reflection into an expository funeral meditation. Changed the 'pagan funeral' comparison into a comparison of named world religions. Added death through sin, Lazarus, new creation, secular naturalism, last judgment, prayer for the dead and ancestor veneration, Islamic judgment, and end-of-life ethics. Corrected references to Westminster Confession 32 and 33 and added Heidelberg and Shorter Catechism anchors where they state the doctrine.
